==Location==
All location tags require coordinates. You can have tags in the brackets [] or you can specify exact locations by yourself. For example, you could use <pre><location[<npc.location>].biome.temperature></pre> to get the temperature at the NPC's location.

{| class="wikitable" width="100%" border="1"
|-
| width="30%" | <location[x,y,z,world].biome.formatted>
| The formatted name of the biome at coordinates.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].biome.humidity>
| The current humidity at the coordinates.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].biome.temperature>
| The current temperature at the coordinates.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].distance[x,y,z,world]>
| The distance between 2 coordinates.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].formatted>
| The coordinates in an easier-to-read format.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].is_liquid>
| Whether or not the block at the coordinates are a liquid. Can be true or false.
|-
| <location[x,y,z,world].light>
| The light level at the coordinates.
|}

==Math Tags==
Math tags are a useful part of Denizen that, as the name implies, allows you to perform mathematical operations internally.

Here's the general syntax, with spaces for readability. (You shouldn't include spaces in your actual script. If you must, put it in "quotes")
<pre>
<m: firstThing + secondThing> 
//Now, all together,
<m:firstThing+secondThing>
</pre>
Of course, + isn't the only mathematical operator that can be used. You can also use:

Minus and Modulus: (- and %)

Divide and Multiply: (/ and *)
